findings.title: Test named for docType value enforcement asserts nothing of the kind
findings.description: The last test in the "squadron machine-artifact docTypes (#73)" block is named "a wrong docType literal is still caught by the value-constraint logic". Every assertion in it is `toHaveLength(0)`. It validates `devlog`, `gate-evidence` and an unknown docType, and all three come back clean. The `mismatched` variable is just a valid `gate-evidence` document. Nothing here exercises a failing `values` check, so the test passes whether or not the constraint works. The comments describe a guarantee the test doesn't provide. Replace it with a case that should fail, for example a schema-registered docType whose `docType` field holds a different value. Alternatively, delete it, since the three "validates clean" tests already cover the happy path.

findings.title: Silent fallback and loosely typed output in the validate command
findings.description: `SEVERITY_ICON` is typed `Record<string, string>` and read as `SEVERITY_ICON[finding.severity] ?? '?'` (line 62). This is a silent placeholder fallback that the project rules forbid. `finding.severity` is a closed union (`'error' | 'warning'`), so key the map on that type, e.g. `Record<FrontmatterFinding['severity'], string>`. The compiler then enforces exhaustiveness and the `?? '?'` goes away. The `colorFn` selection on line 63 has the same flaw. It treats every non-`'error'` severity as a warning, so a new severity would be coloured as a warning without any error. Similarly, `jsonOutput` is built as `Record<string, unknown>` and mutated conditionally for fix mode. A small interface with optional `fixed`, `fixLog` and `fixErrors` would document the JSON contract, which tests and scripts consume.

findings.title: Fix loop applies any fixAction without checking its type
findings.description: The `--fix` loop checks only that `finding.fixAction` exists, then always calls `updateFrontmatterField(field, value)`. The test fixtures give `fixAction` a `type: 'update-frontmatter'` discriminator. If the core service ever emits another action type, this code would apply it as a frontmatter edit without complaint. Either narrow on `fixAction.type`, or add an exhaustive switch so unsupported actions are counted as unfixed. The fix loop also overwrites the file once per finding, so a file with several findings gets several writes and several `dateUpdated` stamps. This is harmless, but it is worth knowing about.

findings.title: validateFrontmatterAction exceeds the function-size guideline
findings.description: `validateFrontmatterAction` is about 75 lines. It handles project resolution, validation, the fix loop and output selection. Extracting `applyFixes(findings, dateStamp)` would cut it under the ~50-line guideline and make the fix logic unit-testable on its own. `printHumanOutput` also does a linear `fixLog.find` per finding. That is fine at this scale.

findings.title: Exit-code handling and schema additions look sound
findings.description: The `handleError(err, exitCode = 1)` extension is backward compatible, because existing callers keep exit code 1. Exit 2 for operational errors versus exit 1 for findings is covered by tests. The three new squadron docType schemas intentionally omit `status` and `dateUpdated`, and the comment explains why. The existing universal-field tests were correctly narrowed to `EXPECTED_DOC_TYPES`. The CLI tests mock core at the module boundary, which is appropriate. I read the first 100 lines of `validate.ts` and did not read the core service implementations, so I haven't checked the behavior of `validateFrontmatterFiles` or `updateFrontmatterField` themselves.

structured_findings.summary: Test named for docType value enforcement asserts nothing of the kind
Silent fallback and loosely typed output in the validate command
Fix loop applies any fixAction without checking its type
Exit-code handling and schema additions look sound
